5._section_summary: This section describes the statistical analyses used: descriptive statistics and Pearson correlations to examine associations among BMI, age, EMWSS, self-compassion (SC), body appreciation (BAS-2), and eating psychopathology (EDE-Q), and path analyses (using AMOS) to test a mediation model with EMWSS as exogenous and SC and BAS-2 as mediators predicting eating psychopathology; BMI and age were included as controls and bootstrap (5,000 samples) bias-corrected CIs were used to assess mediation. The text references a proposed model (Figure 1), but no figure asset was provided.

6.evidence_source: The descriptive statistics for the study variables are presented on Table 1. Correlations analysis' results showed that early memories of warmth and safeness were positively associated to self-compassion and body appreciation, with weak and moderate magnitudes, respectively.
6._section_summary: This section reports correlation results: early memories of warmth and safeness (EMWSS) are positively associated with self-compassion (weak) and body appreciation (moderate), and negatively associated with eating-disorder symptoms (EDE-Q, weak). Self-compassion and body appreciation are positively interrelated and both negatively correlate with EDE-Q. Age showed non-significant associations with body appreciation and EDE-Q, positive correlations with BMI (moderate) and self-compassion (weak), and a negative weak relationship with EMWSS; BMI was negatively associated with EMWSS and body appreciation and positively with EDE-Q (moderate). No study numbering or sample/sample-source details are provided in the text; descriptive statistics are referenced as being in Table 1.

7.evidence_source: The path model was initially tested through a fully saturated model (i.e., with zero degrees of freedom), consisting of 27 parameters.
7._section_summary: This section reports a path analysis testing whether early memories of warmth and safeness affect eating psychopathology severity via self-compassion and body appreciation, controlling for BMI and age. The final trimmed model (after removing nonsignificant paths) showed all remaining standardized paths significant, good model fit, indirect effects (e.g., early memories → EDE-Q indirect effect = -.18), and explained 13% of self-compassion, 34% of body appreciation, and 49% of EDE-Q variance.

8.evidence_source: The text refers to 'this is the first study that examined...' and repeatedly refers to 'the present study', indicating a single study was reported.
8._section_summary: Discussion summarizes a single cross-sectional study (referred to as 'the present study' and 'this is the first study...') that examined links between early memories of warmth/safeness, self-compassion, body appreciation, and eating psychopathology in a nonclinical sample composed only of female participants. The model explained substantial variance in eating psychopathology, with self-compassion and body appreciation mediating the effect of early positive experiences on disordered eating; limitations include cross-sectional design, self-report measures, female-only and nonclinical sample, and lack of generalizability.
